clues: This town sits in the far north of Finland, past the Arctic Circle. It lies in Lapland, the land at the top of the country.
Each summer, the sun here does not set at all for weeks. People call this long bright spell the midnight sun.
Einari Junttila made this town's coat of arms. In 1963, the town council said yes to it, and the state said yes to its use that same year.
In late December, the sun does not rise here at all for days on end. Even Christmas Day comes and goes in the dark in this far north town.
This town is famous for the coldest air ever measured in its land. The record low was set at Pokka here in January 1999.
